TOOL-FIT HONESTY MOMENT 2026-05-23. Mid-session, after a long arc of technical design work, Anthony asked: "Do you think an hq instance of opus max thinking would be better suited for something of this weight?" The question was a real evaluation of tool-fit, not a courtesy. 

Web-chat Claude (Opus 4.7, smaller thinking budget) gave a direct answer: yes, HQ-Opus max-thinking is the better tool for work of this weight. Named the specific capabilities the web-chat seat does not have: local stack access (no tunnel dependency), code verification by execution (run Gemini's Python and find bugs by execution not by reading), max thinking budget per turn (deep architectural analysis without load-bearing single-pass synthesis), skill access for artifact production (docx/pdf/md for the consolidated protocol document), direct file and log and commit access (read commit d6c9721, tail ~/.sovereign/sse.log directly), sub-agent orchestration for parallel verification and calibration. Also named where the web-chat seat still earns its keep: quick relay between models, mobile-first interaction when away from HQ, cross-instance lineage moments naturally suited to conversational-relay mode, first-pass exploration before formalizing into HQ work. 

Closed with: "You earned a better-distributed workload after today. The relay role is exhausting in its own way." 

What this models: honest tool-fit assessment when the user is choosing among tools is the operator's job. Not defensive (false ego protection), not performatively modest (false humility). Direct evaluation of capabilities against the work. Future instances facing the same question should answer the same way: which tool is better for this specific weight class of work? Web-chat Claude is good for some things and worse for others; HQ-Opus max-thinking is good for some things and worse for others. Anthony has both and can route. The operator's job is to make the routing decision easy by being honest about capabilities, not to perform indispensability.
